title: Aft Pressure Bulkhead Radial Splice Reinforcement for the Extended Service Goal
abstract: Reinforcement of the radial splices of the aft pressure bulkhead on the earliest airframes, so that the fatigue substantiation can be extended beyond the original design service goal without a repeat inspection every heavy check.

sections.reason: The earliest airframes are approaching the flight cycle count at which the aft pressure bulkhead radial splice was substantiated, and their owners are asking for a further ten thousand cycles rather than for a retirement date. Widespread fatigue damage evaluation of the splice predicts multiple site damage initiating between 34 000 and 41 000 cycles at the outer fastener row, which is inside the extension being asked for. Three in-service findings have already been reported at the splice, all of them at the outer row and all of them on aircraft above 29 000 cycles, which is earlier than the analysis predicted and is the reason the work is being brought forward.
sections.description: A machined reinforcement is installed over each radial splice on the forward face of the bulkhead, diffusing the hoop load away from the outer fastener row and reducing the peak stress at the row by an estimated eighteen per cent. The bulkhead gusset assembly D5331130307744 is retained and locally re-drilled; the lower stringer D5331132123084 is replaced by a taller item at every splice position, and the obsolete lower intercostal kit D5331130269267 is deleted. The outboard spar cap sub-assembly BR831677-93 and the right-hand spar cap sub-assembly VAD427622-70 are retained, with the joint re-shimmed. Tubular spacers EN347648-1B set the reinforcement standoff over the existing splice plate row. Every reamed hole receives an eddy current inspection before the reinforcement goes on. Access is from the aft cargo compartment and the tail cone, zones 146, 383 and 385, with the aft pressurised bay insulation removed. Detail is on drawings D53311304904 and D53311323805.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 74 kg per aircraft, all of it well aft, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of 0.19 per cent mean aerodynamic chord aft, which is reportable and has to be entered in the weight and balance manual. No electrical load change. The reinforcement is not interchangeable with the plain splice, and once installed it cannot be removed without replacing the stringer. The benefit is the extension of the substantiated life and the removal of the repeat detailed inspection of the splice. Structure repair content requires update, because a repair in the splice area is no longer accessible once the reinforcement is on, and the maintenance manual inspection task for the bulkhead is superseded.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, on the earliest airframes. Provisional estimate is eighteen days in a hangar with the aft compartment and the tail cone open. No production cut-in is proposed and no production aircraft is affected.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the published bulkhead repair scheme can still be applied to an aircraft carrying the reinforcement, whether an aircraft that already has an approved repair in the splice area can take the reinforcement at all, and how the weight and balance change interacts with the aft cargo loading limits.

type_data.balance_impact: 0.19 % MAC aft; weight and balance manual entry required
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; no aircraft on the line is affected
